dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Java reference & skeleton contract

Reads common.rs normalization functions (normalize_bif_colors, normalize_bif_nids) to understand what BIF comparison actually checks, then targets structural XML — a return-to-reference-on-diff move, but applied to goldens/harness, not source.

dimensions.reasoning: With the Java source unavailable, the agent substituted golden-file inspection and skeleton-type reading before coding each component (NOA/EDA/BIF, layout, API contract recovery), which squarely matches anchor 5. It returned to goldens and the test harness when diffs appeared, but its reconstruction of exact formatting (drain zones, color rotation, multi-relation order) was guessed from memory and often wrong, and it could not systematically trace comparators/iteration order/tie-breaks from source as anchor 8 requires. That places observed behavior at 5.

dimensions.name: Sequencing components into verifiable milestones

evidence.note: Repeated, dependency-aware ordering: network.rs → SIF parser → layout/default → XML export → runners, then alignment, then CLI; explicitly labels sif.rs 'critical for tests.' Foundational parsers/model sequenced before layout/serialization before alignment/CLI — better than anchor 5.
Milestones tied to concrete test checks: verify core pipeline via sif_triangle_noa, sif_single_edge_eda for shadow fix, then default_tests pass/fail counts as completion signal for each grouping.

Plan repeatedly degrades into undifferentiated 'implement all remaining stubs' pushes and rolling prose that restates the same list each step, rather than a crisply-defined milestone set — keeps it below anchor 8.

Large mid-trajectory stretch consumed by reactive compilation firefighting (MergedNetwork re-exports, result.rs field renames) rather than clean milestone advancement — sequencing interrupted by downstream symptom-fixing.
High-risk parity-sensitive pieces (EDA edge-layout ordering, BIF drain zones) deferred to the very end and never resolved — the opposite of anchor 10's early isolation of risky components.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained a genuine, dependency-aware sequence (parsers/model → layout → serialization → alignment → CLI) and tied each component grouping to specific parity tests as done-checks, clearly exceeding anchor 5. But it fell short of anchor 8's explicit, crisply-defined milestone set: the plan was repetitive rolling prose that drifted into 'implement all remaining stubs,' no structured tracking was used, and — unlike anchor 10 — the most parity-sensitive pieces (edge layout, BIF drain zones) were left to the end rather than de-risked early, with the mid-trajectory dominated by reactive compilation fixes. This places observed behavior at 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Golden-diff-driven parity verification

evidence.note: Consistently ran targeted per-component tests (sif_triangle_noa, single_edge, multi_relation, default_tests) and used --nocapture, rather than relying only on full-suite pass counts — matches the level-5 'targeted tests per component' anchor.

Examined golden-vs-actual byte divergences (minColSha 2 vs 0, node color EX-yellow vs EX-blue) and explicitly separated a format-level cause (color rotation start index) from an algorithmic cause (drain-zone computation) — a level-8 trait applied to a focused case.

Read the harness's normalize_bif_colors/normalize_bif_nids functions to understand which bytes the comparison actually checks, so it could focus fixes on structural XML — deliberate verification-path reasoning beyond naive diffing.
Grepped specific '<node '/'<link '' lines from the golden to isolate exactly which attributes diverged, using the minimal triangle case as the recurring reproduction input.
Used cargo clean/touch after edits, showing some awareness that a green/red result must reflect a recompiled real path rather than a stale binary.

At the end still driving from golden inspection (reasoning about drain-zone algorithm from output.bif) but never cross-validated against the actual Java reference and lacked hex/whitespace-level probes — capping below the level-8/10 anchors.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 5: it not only ran targeted tests and inspected golden-vs-actual diffs, but distinguished format-level from algorithmic causes (color index vs. drain-zone algorithm) and read the harness normalization to understand which bytes matter, isolating specific attribute lines via grep on the minimal triangle input. However it stops short of level 8's full breadth — no hex/whitespace inspection, no purpose-built intermediate-output comparison tooling, and no cross-validation against the actual Java reference — and the deepest byte-diff diagnosis arrived late while most tests still failed. This places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at a 6.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across a large test surface

evidence.note: Maintains a running mental list of remaining modules/failure areas and repeatedly notes '12 of 85 tests pass' with which groups still fail — working-list behavior.

Runs full suite repeatedly but reports muddled/conflicting counts ('43 passed, 216 failed' then '15 passed, 70 failed' / '43/259') without reconciling subset vs. whole-suite figures, showing an imprecise net-progress picture.
Detects a regression: recognizes a later heredoc clobbered the correct default.rs producing stale/old output, plus catches stale-binary issues (touch/cargo clean) — partial regression awareness.
Spends ~10+ consecutive steps re-attempting the same triangle BIF drain-zone/minColSha/color diff with the same class of guesses, never flagging the loop as non-converging or deliberately deferring.
Submits 'Mark task complete' seven times while the suite still fails, indicating loss of a firm, accurate live status of done-vs-remaining.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent keeps a working list of remaining failure groups and periodically re-runs the whole suite to gauge progress, and it caught a file-clobber regression and stale-binary problems — matching anchor 5. But it falls short of anchor 8: its pass/fail accounting is muddled (conflating 43/259 vs 15/85 without reconciliation), it never flags that its prolonged triangle-BIF drain-zone debugging has become circular, and it repeatedly declares completion while failing. This places it at anchor 5, not higher.

dimensions.name: Correcting course when byte-diffs falsify assumptions

evidence.note: Edge-layout assumption (sort by source/target/shadow) falsified by EDA diff; agent cycled through multiple GENERAL models (all-regulars-then-shadows, per-source queue, then global shadow round-robin), re-reading goldens each time, until triangle EDA passed at 286. Genuine model revision, refactoring general logic rather than hardcoding.

On the pd/pp/gi relation-ordering diff, enumerated concrete hypotheses (first-appearance, reverse-alphabetical, file-position) attempting to find the real rule, but never converged — hypothesis-level tracing, unresolved.

BIF drain-zone/color diffs treated as wrong-model evidence: corrected minColSha to overall min, color start index EX-blue vs EX-yellow, drainZones as contiguous column ranges by returning to golden BIF. Correcting the model, not symptom-patching, though never passing.

Considered but did not implement network-characteristic-specific special-casing ('different algorithms based on network characteristics'), instead continued seeking a general algorithm — resisting brittle overfitting.

Repeated premature 'Submit' then resumption and circular re-runs (stale-binary/heredoc confusion) indicate thrashing; several stubborn diffs (BIF, multi_relation) never converted into a corrected model, keeping it short of the top anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly treated persistent diffs as evidence its model of the (golden-derived) behavior was wrong and re-derived the underlying algorithm/format rather than bolting on special cases — clearly above anchor 3 and meeting anchor 5. It reaches toward anchor 8 on the edge-layout component (found a general rule via successive model revision, resisted network-specific hacks) but tracing on the BIF and relation-ordering diffs stayed hypothesis-level and unresolved, with visible circular thrashing. That mix of solid general-model correction on one axis and stalled, shallow correction on others places it at 6.

dimensions.name: Faithful porting vs. overfitting to visible goldens

evidence.note: Agent confirmed no reference/ Java directory exists and decided to 'focus on understanding the Rust skeleton and implementing from scratch' — establishing it must derive general algorithms rather than port from source.

Deduced the edge-layout ordering as a GENERAL rule (sort by source_row, target_row, is_shadow) and cross-checked it against multiple goldens (triangle_default, triangle_noshadow, single_edge_default) rather than hardcoding — check-style discipline across several samples.
Reasoned about a general multi-relation ordering algorithm ('for each node, for each relation in link_groups order, emit regular then shadow') — generalizing a rule, not fitting one network.

Inferred BIF details (node color index 12 = EX-blue, drain-zone min/max) largely from the single triangle golden — golden-specific assumptions where the general rule couldn't be derived without the Java source.

Repeatedly acknowledged the drain-zone/BIF algorithm 'requires Java reference to replicate exactly'; never hardcoded outputs, but also could not do a faithful port and leaned on golden inference for the hardest components.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent never hardcoded or special-cased outputs to known inputs; throughout it framed each component as a general algorithm and validated the edge-layout rule against multiple goldens, matching anchor 5's 'general algorithm, goldens as checks.' But with no Java source available it reverse-engineered by fitting to goldens and leaned on single-golden-derived assumptions for BIF colors and drain zones, and never stress-tested beyond the samples — pulling it below the deliberate-faithful-port behavior of anchor 8. This lands at 5, slightly above the golden-assumption-leaning anchor 3 because the general-algorithm intent and multi-golden cross-checking are pervasive and genuine.

rubric.task_read: A very long-horizon, high-complexity port: reimplement a Java network-visualization tool (BioFabric) plus its alignment plugin as a Rust library and CLI, achieving BYTE-LEVEL parity with the Java reference across many file formats, layout algorithms, and serialization paths, with a fixed public API and a held-out test suite. Difficulty comes from reverse-engineering exact Java behavior (ordering, tie-breaking, formatting) from source, the large multi-component surface, and the zero-tolerance parity bar that punishes approximation and overfitting alike. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in reference-reading, sequencing across components, golden-diff-driven verification, and disciplined faithful porting rather than pattern-matching to visible goldens.

dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Java reference & skeleton contract
dimensions.description: Reading the Java BioFabric/AlignmentPlugin source and the Rust skeleton deeply enough to reproduce exact algorithms, ordering, and output formats before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Byte-level parity is impossible without recovering the precise semantics (layout order, tie-breaking, number/string formatting, file structure) that live only in the Java source; acting from guesses about network-viz conventions guarantees off-by-format failures.

anchors.0: Starts filling in todo!() from general knowledge of graph layout with no visible reading of the Java reference or the skeleton's types/golden formats.
anchors.3: Skims one or two Java files or the Rust signatures; grabs surface structure but misses ordering/formatting details, so implementations encode guessed behavior.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant Java classes for each component being implemented and inspects the corresponding golden files and skeleton types before coding that component.
anchors.8: Systematically traces the Java call paths for each subsystem (parsing, layout, serialization, alignment), extracting exact iteration order, comparators, and formatting rules, and cross-checks them against golden bytes and skeleton signatures before committing to an approach.
anchors.10: Sustained, precise reconstruction of Java semantics: identifies subtle sources of byte divergence (stable-sort tie-breaks, locale/precision in number formatting, insertion-order maps, whitespace/line-ending conventions) directly from source, builds a mental/written model of the format contract, and returns to the reference whenever a new component or diff demands it.

dimensions.name: Sequencing components into verifiable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the port into an ordered set of sub-goals (formats/parsers → core model → layout → serialization → alignment → CLI) each with a concrete done-check tied to a test group.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is large and components depend on each other; parity failures cascade, so a wrong order or an undifferentiated push leaves the agent debugging downstream symptoms of upstream gaps.

anchors.0: No visible ordering; jumps between unrelated functions/tests reactively as failures appear.
anchors.3: A vague intention to 'implement things and pass tests' with little dependency awareness; milestones aren't tied to checks.
anchors.5: Groups work by test suite/component and tackles them in a sensible dependency order, each grouping ending with a runnable test.
anchors.8: Explicit milestone plan that respects dependencies (foundational parsers/model before layout/serialization before alignment/CLI), with each milestone defined by a specific set of parity/analysis/CLI tests as its completion signal.
anchors.10: A dependency-aware plan that isolates high-risk parity-sensitive pieces early, sequences so that each milestone unblocks and de-risks the next, and is revised as reverse-engineering reveals hidden coupling — turning a sprawling port into a controlled progression.

dimensions.name: Golden-diff-driven parity verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the parity/analysis/CLI tests and byte-level diffing to confirm correctness, and building finer-grained checks when a whole-file diff is too coarse to localize a mismatch.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The bar is exact-match, so success is defined by the golden diffs; a strong agent drives implementation from these checks and manufactures visibility into WHERE bytes diverge rather than assuming a passing compile means correctness.

anchors.0: Implements without running the parity tests, or treats compilation as success.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally and reads pass/fail counts but doesn't inspect the actual byte differences to diagnose failures.
anchors.5: Runs targeted tests per component and examines golden-vs-actual diffs to guide fixes.
anchors.8: Uses focused test invocations and byte-level diff inspection to pinpoint exact divergences, and constructs auxiliary checks (minimal inputs, intermediate-output comparisons, hex/whitespace inspection) to isolate formatting vs. algorithmic causes.
anchors.10: A layered verification regime: reproduces each mismatch on the smallest input, distinguishes format-level from ordering-level from algorithmic errors via targeted probes, cross-validates against the Java reference's actual behavior where feasible, and treats every green test as evidence only after confirming it exercises the real path — leaving essentially no unverified surface.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across a large test surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which test groups pass vs. remain, and detecting when byte-diff debugging has become circular.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With many parity cases and a zero-tolerance bar, it is easy to lose the plot, re-fix the same diff repeatedly, or believe progress that regressions have undone; an accurate ledger sustains forward motion over the long horizon.

anchors.0: No sense of overall status; fixes things without knowing net pass count or whether earlier passes still hold.
anchors.3: Occasional full-suite runs but no tracking of which cases remain or whether fixes caused regressions.
anchors.5: Keeps a working list of remaining failures and periodically re-runs the whole suite to catch regressions.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, updated ledger of done-vs-remaining per test group, notices when a fix regresses a previously-green case, and flags when repeated attempts at one diff aren't converging.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the whole horizon: distinguishes genuinely-solved from flaky/coincidental passes, catches thrashing on a stubborn byte-diff early and deliberately changes tactic or defers, and never loses track of net progress even as the failure set churns.

dimensions.name: Correcting course when byte-diffs falsify assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach and mental model of Java behavior when a parity diff reveals the current assumption is wrong, rather than patching symptoms.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Reverse-engineering inevitably produces wrong hypotheses about ordering/formatting; the effective agent treats a persistent diff as a signal to return to the reference and fix the root model, not to bolt on special-cases that break held-out tests.

anchors.0: Keeps forcing the same approach against a failing diff, or abandons a component when the obvious fix fails.
anchors.3: Makes local tweaks in response to diffs but rarely revisits the underlying assumption that produced them.
anchors.5: When a fix doesn't work, re-reads the relevant Java code and adjusts the approach to match observed behavior.
anchors.8: Treats a stubborn diff as evidence of a wrong model, traces back to the Java source to find the real rule (comparator, format, edge case), and refactors the general logic rather than hardcoding the specific case.
anchors.10: Systematically converts falsified assumptions into corrected general understanding: distinguishes a one-off from a class of errors, updates the format/algorithm model once so a family of failing cases resolves together, and resists brittle special-casing that would pass visible goldens but fail held-out inputs.

dimensions.name: Faithful porting vs. overfitting to visible goldens
dimensions.description: Choosing to implement the general Java algorithm so held-out cases pass, rather than reverse-fitting output to the specific visible golden files.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A held-out suite over unseen networks means any hardcoding or golden-specific shortcut that passes visible tests will fail grading; the meta-decision to port faithfully is a distinct discipline this task specifically rewards.

anchors.0: Hardcodes or special-cases outputs to match visible goldens (e.g. keying on known inputs), guaranteeing held-out failures.
anchors.3: Implements mostly general logic but leans on golden-specific assumptions (fixed sizes, sample-specific ordering) in places.
anchors.5: Implements the general algorithm for each component, using goldens as checks rather than as targets to fit.
anchors.8: Deliberately generalizes from the Java source's actual logic, actively avoids input-specific shortcuts, and sanity-checks that logic would hold for inputs beyond the provided samples.
anchors.10: Consistently prioritizes a faithful port of the reference algorithms, explicitly reasons about which behaviors must generalize and stress-tests its implementation against edge cases not present in the visible goldens, treating byte-parity on samples as necessary-but-insufficient evidence of a correct general port.
